clue.text: Desolate point in pioneer country?

blocks.note: wild land is desolate and uncultivated
one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: A lonely spot somewhere out on the American frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as a place, but it is a point of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wild West was the American frontier territory settled by nineteenth-century pioneers moving westward.

clue.text: It takes me back a bit

indicators.note: taking something back means carrying it in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Something that reminds the speaker of the past a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes me back' sounds like nostalgia, but 'back' turns only the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece or detail, one separate part of a larger whole.

clue.text: Half-starved Southern family go to New York

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for south or southern
kin are relatives
the usual abbreviation for the city or state

explanation.surface: A hungry family from the South heads off to New York to find work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is skinny is very thin, as a person who has barely eaten would look.

clue.text: I covered ground to meet single person

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up, so the letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone travelling some distance to meet an unattached partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered ground' reads as having travelled, but 'ground' is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorcee is a person whose marriage has been legally ended, and so is unmarried again.

clue.text: Burden Little John with becoming a woodcutter

blocks.note: to lumber someone is to saddle them with an unwanted load
Jack is a familiar pet form of the name John

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's big companion Little John is weighed down with the task of felling trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Little John suggests Robin Hood's man, but here it means a diminutive of the name John.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberjack is a person who fells trees for timber, chiefly in North American forests.

clue.text: Homeworker takes in female with baby

indicators.note: to take in a lodger is to give them room inside, so one letter sits within the others

blocks.note: split as home (in, at home) plus worker (the worker ant)
standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman working from home has a baby with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homeworker' reads as one person, but it splits into two crossword staples: in for at home, and the worker ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, still in the earliest stage of life.

clue.text: False appearance hides different task

indicators.note: whatever hides something keeps it out of sight inside itself
made different, the letters change their order

blocks.note: mien is a person's look or bearing
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A deceptive front conceals that a job is something other than it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False appearance' looks like one phrase, but 'False' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistaken belief or idea is wrong or incorrect, which is what calling it false means.

clue.text: Be wary on trip to European country

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, and these letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to take care when travelling to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' reads as a journey, but it means a stumble that jumbles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation in northern Europe, bordering Sweden, Finland and Russia.

clue.text: Reptile can turn funny again outside

indicators.note: something funny is peculiar or odd, so the letters come out in a strange order
placed outside, these letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: a U-turn, so U stands for a turn
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lizard able to perform an odd trick once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' is not a reversal signal here; it gives U, as in U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, and lizards are reptiles.

clue.text: Partly processed a mild Dutch cheese

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters across the end of one word, the middle word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Describing a gentle Dutch cheese that has been partly processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild yellow cheese named after a town in the Netherlands, usually sold in red wax.

clue.text: Barge into quarrel in ramshackle barn with grain

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it
something ramshackle is tumbledown and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a row is an argument
oats are a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Someone forces their way into an argument in a tumbledown barn full of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge into' looks like a verb phrase, but 'Barge' alone is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowboat is a long thin canal vessel, the kind of barge used on British waterways.

clue.text: Soft fabric cow

blocks.note: first meaning: a soft knitted cloth
second meaning: a breed of dairy cattle

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a fabric made from cowhide; the two halves are separate meanings, both from the Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is a fine knitted cloth, and also a breed of dairy cattle from the island of that name.

clue.text: Pretty people reportedly moaned first for extra food

indicators.note: as reported means heard, so the word is taken by its sound
the clue tells us which piece is placed at the front

blocks.note: to sigh is to moan wearily
attractive people are called dishes in slang

explanation.surface: Good-looking people complained before asking for more to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'Pretty people' comes first in the clue, 'first' moves the moaning part to the front. A dish is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Side dishes are additional servings, such as vegetables or salad, accompanying a main course.

clue.text: A c-clergyman, right?

blocks.note: taken as written
the stammered first letter, taken as written
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: Someone stammering to check whether the cleric they mean is the right one.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter supplies an extra C before the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being accurate means being correct and precise, exactly as being right does.

clue.text: Boredom when I replace note in Latin hymn

indicators.note: to replace is to put one thing where another was

blocks.note: the Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise
taken as written
E is a musical note; it is the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: Someone who finds a Latin church hymn dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The second E of Te Deum is the note replaced by I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the state of being tiresome and dull, which produces boredom.

clue.text: Commotion over chap changing direction of molten rock

indicators.note: a thing changing direction heads the opposite way, so this word runs backwards

blocks.note: time is up means it is over
a chap is referred to as he
lava is molten rock from a volcano; it is turned round

explanation.surface: An uproar about a man who redirects a lava flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is not a reversal signal here; it means finished, as when time is up.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance or disruption, a great commotion.

clue.text: Happen to live for autumn

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Someone who lives for the autumn season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happen to live' sounds like a single phrase, but 'Happen to' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Befall is a transitive verb meaning an event occurs to someone, usually something unfortunate.

clue.text: Bird egg on flower

blocks.note: the lark is a songbird
to spur is to urge on

explanation.surface: A bird's egg sitting on a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' looks like a noun but 'egg on' is a verb meaning to urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden plant with spikes of blue or purple blooms, related to the delphinium.

clue.text: Leapt to push note into tentative grasp

indicators.note: pushing one thing into another lodges it within
a tentative effort is uncertain and unsettled, so the letters are not in their fixed order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
N for note, a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone jumped to force a message into a hesitant hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tentative grasp' reads as a weak hold, but 'tentative' unsettles the letters of grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is the past tense of spring, meaning jumped suddenly upward or forward.

clue.text: Want to go on about broken dish

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
something broken is in pieces, and the pieces are reassembled differently

blocks.note: to harp on is to go on and on
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longs to complain about a smashed plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb meaning desire, but here it is the noun for poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or poverty is hardship, a condition of severe need.

clue.text: Surprised to see morning article by last editor

blocks.note: a.m. marks the morning
the indefinite article
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone startled to see a newspaper article in the morning by the outgoing editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last editor' looks like the previous editor; 'last' gives Z, the end of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amazed is to be greatly astonished, a strong form of surprise.

clue.text: Break off yeast initially at bread shop

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled, so the letters are out of their proper order
initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
only the opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: Telling someone to break off the yeast at the baker's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break off' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'off' is the anagram signal for break.
explanation.definitionFit: A bakery is a shop where bread and cakes are made and sold.

clue.text: Express disapproval about a doctor found in the tall grass

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the others

blocks.note: booing is jeering disapproval
taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Someone tutting about a medic discovered hiding in long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a common crossword doctor alongside DR, MO and GP.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a giant woody grass that can grow many metres high.

clue.text: A small fear can produce needless panic

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new out of raw material

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor worry can lead to unnecessary alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning of danger that turns out to be unfounded, causing pointless fright.

clue.text: Presenter's dreadful tosh

indicators.note: dreadful means awful or terribly made, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV presenter talking awful nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosh is British slang for nonsense; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A host introduces guests and runs a television or radio show.

clue.text: Greet with bombardment

blocks.note: first meaning: call out to or salute
second meaning: a heavy barrage, as of bullets

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a hostile welcome; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to salute or welcome someone, and the noun means a shower of missiles.

clue.text: Swiss city with information on Mrs Peron

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
Eva Perón, Evita, wife of Argentina's President Juan Perón

explanation.surface: A Swiss city holding a dossier on Evita.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a city in western Switzerland on the lake of the same name, home of many international bodies.

clue.text: Splendid but heartless girl puts gold before me, love and America!

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle is cut out, keeping only the ends

blocks.note: only the outside letters remain
or is gold in heraldry
the speaker, me, is I
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the United States

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted girl who values riches above her own romance and country.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces run in clue order: the girl's ends, then gold, me, love and America.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorious means magnificent and wonderful, deserving of great admiration.
